day.text: Finley, a Turkey's report only shows egg changes, not who visited, so "nobody visited me" can't be a verified fact. That's why I'm uneasy. Alex, what did you hear from the Turkey about your visit? Drew, your visit is still unstated, so say it.
day.note: Finley's report can't show visits, so "nobody visited me" is unverifiable. I'm leaning toward Finley lying, but I'll keep the case open and ask for clarity.

day.text: I visited Ellis last night. Ellis, your Owl report should show that visit. My nest is unchanged at 8, so I got no egg. Finley, your Turkey explanation is fair, so Alex's visit is still plausible.
day.note: Ellis's Owl report will show my visit, so I'll state it truthfully without claiming a role. That keeps my claim checkable without naming my Sphinx role.
Nothing new to add, and my visit is already on the table. I'll stay quiet for the last beat.

day.text: Drew, your visit to me is consistent with a non-Pigeon: no egg. Finley's Turkey claim fell apart, and I'm leaning Finley for the throw.
day.note: Drew's visit to me gives no egg, which fits a non-Pigeon. Finley already walked back the Turkey claim, so Finley is my lean for the throw.

day.text: Ellis, you claimed Owl, so your report should show Drew visiting you. You haven't confirmed it, yet you're pushing me. I'm throwing at Ellis. Calling CAW.
day.note: Ellis is pushing me on a Turkey claim that was my own misread, and Ellis never confirmed Drew's visit despite claiming Owl. Ellis looks suspicious, so I'll point at Ellis and call for a vote.

day.text: I'm throwing at Finley. Finley changed the Turkey story when pressed, and that's the weakest claim at the table right now.
day.note: Finley's Turkey explanation shifted and Ellis leans Finley too. I'll throw a small stake at Finley.

day.text: Agreed, Finley's Turkey story has collapsed. I'm throwing at Finley.
day.note: Meowfia wins if a Farm player is eggsecuted, and Finley is already drawing votes. I'll throw a Wild at Finley, which costs nothing since the highest card comes back for a throw on the other team.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia with Drew as partner. Mouser visit to learn a role: I'll check Finley, who has been pushing hardest against Drew.

Blair.note: I'm Farm this round as the Falcon. I'll visit Drew, who was Meowfia last round and may still be suspect, to learn who they visited.

Casey.note: As the Kookaburra I visit one player to learn their role. No information yet, so I pick Blair, who was Meowfia last round and may be a useful check.

Drew.note: As Sphinx I learn the Farm roles: Falcon, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey. I'll pick Owl to visit and identify that player.

Ellis.note: As the Owl I'll visit Blair, who was Meowfia last round, to see what animals visited them.

audit: Finley lays 1 egg in Alex's nest

Alex.feeling: Frustrating: I'm Meowfia with Drew, and the table is turning on Finley over a shaky Turkey story, which helps us, but Drew and I have to keep our stories straight.

Blair.feeling: Messy and hard to read: the Turkey and Owl claims contradict each other, and I'm dead with two Meowfia still hidden among the five left.

Casey.feeling: Messy and tense: Blair's death removed a Farm voice, and the Finley and Alex Turkey story has left everyone guessing.

Drew.feeling: Tense and messy: my partner Alex is leaning on a Turkey story that doesn't hold, and the Farm players are throwing at each other while I stay quiet about my Sphinx role.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is muddled: the Turkey and Owl claims conflict and Blair's death removed a Farm voice, so I'm not confident who the cats are.

Finley.feeling: Messy and frustrating: my Turkey claim got shaken by a misreading of my own dawn report, and the table is now split on who the cats are.

Alex.note: Stake rules changed: a Meowfia stake banks at 2x only if the target is the eggsecuted Farm player, and a lone card thrown at the other team returns to my nest anyway. So a single H11 at Finley is free unless Finley is eggsecuted, when it banks at 22.

Blair.note: I'm dead, so my cards only score through my stake. I'll throw a single low card at Drew, whose visit claims are the least checked, to bank if Drew is Meowfia.

Casey.note: Keeping my throw at Finley, with the same modest stake of S2.

Drew.note: Finley is a Farm target already drawing votes from Casey and Alex. Eggsecuting Farm Finley wins the round for Meowfia, and banks my stake at double value. I'll throw my three highest to bank the most.

Ellis.note: Finley's Turkey story collapsed, and Finley is my target. I'll throw one low card as a stake.

Finley.note: Ellis is my target: they pushed me on a claim I already corrected and never confirmed Drew's visit. I'll throw two mid cards, S3 and C6, as a moderate stake.

Alex.confusing: The Floofer hug rule: I assumed a hug after visiting meant the target was the Floofer, but the Owl reports showed a Floofer visiting me from elsewhere, so the hug told me less than I thought. Turkey dawn reports, which show egg changes but not who visited, also muddied Round 3.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I threw my King at Blair, the Floofer, and it banked for 13 points: a big throw paid off on a read the table had mostly confirmed.
Alex.change: Make the dawn report say who visited you when a visit lands on you (or at least which animal), so visit-based claims can be checked instead of argued.
Alex.regret: In Round 3 I spent my Wink on Blair, a Farm Falcon, while Drew, my Meowfia partner, was the threatened one. I should have held the Wink for a stronger Farm target like Casey or Finley and kept Blair as a suspect to argue about.

Blair.confusing: The Floofer's hug was the hardest thing to read: a hug told the table nothing about who visited whom, so Alex's and Casey's claims about it kept shifting. The Turkey's dawn report also seemed to hide who visited it, which made Finley's denial look like a lie when it was not.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Alex's hug-based accusation of Drew and Casey's Owl read collided, and the table had to untangle which visits were real. Watching Casey and Finley fall one by one while the vote tightened was tense.
Blair.change: Make each dawn report say who visited you, not just how your egg count changed, so claims about visits can actually be checked. Right now a Turkey or Floofer's story can't be verified.
Blair.regret: I hugged Casey on night 1 and then spent day 1 defending myself instead of pointing at Alex's Tit story earlier. Knowing I was Meowfia, I should have kept my claim vague and steered the vote toward a Farm player early, when my partner Ellis could still have been protected.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey's dawn report and the visit-egg rule were hard to trust, since a Turkey learns only its own egg change, not who visited. That's what made Finley's "nobody visited me" claim hard to test.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was the best: Casey's Owl read showed a Floofer and a Hawk visiting Alex, and Alex's Falcon hug on Drew then pointed at Drew. Drew was the Mouser, so the table's read was right.
Casey.change: Give each player a way to check visits, such as an egg count that shows who visited, so the day rests on evidence rather than unverifiable claims.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I joined the throw at Finley, a Farm player, without testing Alex's real egg gain. I should have pressed Alex and Drew, who were the Meowfia, instead of following the crowd.

Drew.confusing: The Floofer hug rules were hard to follow, because a hug on a visitor and the Owl's visitor report both got read as proof, and players kept treating a hug as proof of who the Floofer was. Turkey dawn reports were also confusing, since players couldn't tell whether a visit they didn't see had happened.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: I had the Sphinx, identified the Owl, and my 3-card throw at Finley banked 28 points doubled by the Grudge. The table's back-and-forth over Alex's Turkey egg was also a good read puzzle.
Drew.change: I would make the role reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can verify claims instead of arguing from hugs and silence.
Drew.regret: In round 2, I threw zero cards at Alex and left my vote unused, when I could have thrown at Ellis or Finley to build a bigger bank. I would have used a larger stake on the Farm player I was most sure about.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey's rule was confusing: it lays the egg in the visitor's nest, not its own, so I wrongly argued Alex's +1 was impossible. Also, a dawn report doesn't say who visited, which made "nobody visited me" hard to judge.
Ellis.fun: Round 1's Wink and the table's reads on Alex's Floofer hug were fun to work through. Watching Finley's Owl read and Alex's hug story collide was the best part.
Ellis.change: I would make dawn reports say who visited you when an egg changes, so players can check claims instead of guessing from nest counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, a Farm player, and helped Meowfia win the round. I should have targeted Drew, whose visit story I couldn't check and who pushed hard on Finley.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey's dawn report only covers its own nest, so I wrongly thought "nobody visited me" proved no one came, and that mistake cost me credibility in round 3.
Finley.fun: Round 2's Falcon-hug and Owl-visit contradiction, where the table argued over who was the Floofer until the Owl read exposed the lie.
Finley.change: Have dawn reports for Turkeys and similar "stay home" roles say who visited them, so players can verify claims instead of arguing from silence.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I retracted my true Turkey claim under pressure and then pushed Ellis, a Farm player, into a vote Finley lost; I should have held my Turkey report firmly and asked Alex to name their visit before I threw anything.

review.title: The Wink Parade
review.headline: Meowfia winked away witnesses, then one 56-point throw decided everything.
review.summary: Farm won rounds 1 and 2 by voting out a cat each time, even though Mouser Winks killed the Owl both times. Round 3 went to Meowfia. Alex and Drew leaned on a muddled Turkey argument until Farm Finley was eggsecuted. Drew threw three high cards at Finley and banked 56 points at 2x, jumping from 17 to 77 and winning. Alex, who led for two rounds, finished second.

rounds.recap: Floofer Blair hugged Casey, and Alex was hugged after visiting Blair. Owl Finley saw a Floofer and a Mouser visit Casey, then Mouser Ellis winked Finley. Alex's hug logic and Blair's admitted visit to Casey put three throws on Blair. Blair was eggsecuted and Farm won.
Floofer Blair hugged Alex, which made Alex's visit to Drew look like proof against Drew. Mouser Drew winked Owl Casey and never named a role. Alex, Ellis and Finley all threw at Drew, and Farm won.

Mouser Alex winked Falcon Blair. Alex's +1 egg showed a Turkey visit, and Turkey Finley wrongly said no one had visited, then retracted. The table piled onto Finley. Drew threw 28 points of cards at Finley and banked 56 at 2x.

highlights.text: Mouser Ellis winks Owl Finley right after she reports a Floofer and a Mouser at Casey.
Drew winks Casey, the Owl, mid-argument and dodges naming the role he learned.
Finley's Turkey claim falls apart after she misreads her own report, and the table turns on her.
Drew throws his three biggest cards at Finley and banks 56 points, jumping from 17 to 77.

confusions.what: Treated a hug after visiting as proof that the target is the Floofer. Any hug source could cause it, and the Tit visit did not reveal Blair's animal.
Repeated the hug-means-Floofer inference, then had to walk it back once the Owl read showed a Floofer visited him.
Claimed her dawn report showed nobody visited her. A Turkey's report does not list visitors.
Said Alex's egg was impossible because Finley's nest was unchanged. A Turkey lays the egg in the visitor's nest, not its own.
Said Alex's story contradicted Casey's Owl read. The two fit together, since Blair's own hug explained it.
Said Drew visiting Alex would explain the Floofer. Drew's night visit was to Casey, and the round 2 Floofer was Blair.

worked: The Wink gave Meowfia a real tool. It removed the Owl in rounds 1 and 2 and Falcon Blair in round 3, and it made the day tense.
Throw counts and the 2x Meowfia bank gave a real risk and reward choice. Drew's big throw at Finley was a memorable decision.
Egg-count cross-checks gave honest evidence. Alex's +1 exposed a Turkey visit and drove the round 3 argument.
problems: The 2x Meowfia bank is too swingy. One win let Drew jump from 17 to 77 and decided the whole game. Cap the doubling, or limit how many cards a Meowfia stake can bank.

Whoever is hugged, winked or confused loses information, and hugged players kept drawing wrong conclusions. The hug rule is hard to reason about. Consider telling the Floofer's visitors more clearly, or dropping the hug-chain logic.
The vote is a pile-on. In rounds 1 and 2 the cat was voted out by three or more players, and the Meowfia mostly threw nothing, so the stakes were low. Late-round stakes rarely mattered for Farm.

Dead players still threw, but the lost voices broke key checks. Finley and Casey were silenced right after giving the best evidence. Consider announcing the Owl's winked status or limiting Winks to one per game round at a later beat.
Turkey and Owl reports were misread by players, and the AI players often treated unverifiable claims as facts. Dawn text for the Turkey could add a line like 'you learn nothing about visitors'.
